name: Rattenberg
kurzbeschreibung: The tiniest town in Austria with a medieval ambiance and home to Tirol’s only glassblowing workshop.
text:
Überblick

Rattenberg is situated in the Tyrolean Lower Inn Valley within the Kufstein district at an elevation of 514 metres directly on the southern banks of the Inn River. Covering a mere 0.11 square kilometres with around 450 residents, Rattenberg is officially the smallest town in Austria by land area and the least populated with town privileges. Wedged between the steep Schlossberg castle hill and the river, the town showcases a remarkably preserved medieval townscape in the regional Inn-Salzach architectural style. Gabled townhouses with pastel facades line the entirely pedestrianised historic core. Rattenberg is globally renowned as Austria's premier Glass Town, celebrated for artistic glassmaking and historic craft culture.

Geschichte

The settlement developed under the protection of a 10th-century stronghold built by the Counts of Rattenberg, with its first written mention dating to 1254 in the Treaty of Erharting. Thanks to its key location controlling river navigation and tolls between Bavaria and Tyrol, Duke Stephen III of Bavaria-Ingolstadt granted Rattenberg city status in 1393. During the War of the Succession of Landshut in 1504, Emperor Maximilian I captured the stronghold, incorporating it into Tyrol. Prosperity expanded through river shipping and regional silver mining. Following the Second World War, displaced Bohemian master glassblowers and engravers, particularly the Kisslinger family, established artisanal workshops. Since 1946, Kisslinger Kristallglas has thrived as an international hallmark. The 14th-century Augustinian monastery now houses the prestigious Augustinian Museum with Gothic sacred art and an accessible church tower.

Anreise

Rattenberg provides superb transport infrastructure. By car, visitors travel along the Inntalautobahn A12 to the Kramsach/Alpbachtal exit and follow the B171 for just one kilometre. Because the entire historic old town is pedestrianised, spacious parking areas (P1 to P4) with electric charging stations are situated right beside the town gates. Train travellers arrive effortlessly at the Rattenberg-Kramsach station on the Lower Inn Valley railway. S-Bahn Tirol trains (line S8) stop every half hour, and the town centre is a pleasant three-minute walk away through the historic southern gate.

Tipps

A stop at the Kisslinger Kristallglas glassworks offers an exceptional experience watching craftsmen shape molten crystal glass beside roaring 1,200-degree furnaces, with guests even invited to blow their own glass bauble. The Augustinian Museum features rare Gothic sculptures and Tyrol's only climbable church bell tower with 360-degree views of the Inn River. A gentle path climbs the Schlossberg to the ruins of Rattenberg Castle, home to open-air productions of the renowned Tiroler Schlossbergspiele theatrical festival in summer. During Advent, the candlelit Rattenberger Advent illuminates the alleys exclusively with thousands of candles, torches, and wood fires without any electric lights.
